subject.title: feat: MCP Apps (ui://) Phase 0 — generic host in Control UI + plugin-declared MCP servers

question: Should native OpenClaw plugin manifests permanently declare executable `mcpServers`, with user configuration overriding same-named servers, disabled plugins detaching them, and relative stdio paths resolving from the plugin root?
rationale: Tests and direct dependency inspection establish that the implementation works, but they cannot decide whether executable MCP server activation belongs in the long-term public plugin manifest contract.

options.title: Approve the manifest contract
options.body: Accept the combined PR and treat the documented declaration, precedence, disablement, relative-path, and cross-runtime behavior as the supported plugin API.

options.title: Split `mcpServers`
options.body: Land the generic MCP Apps host and durable storage while moving the public executable plugin declaration into a separately reviewed PR.

options.title: Pause Phase 0
options.body: Keep the entire feature open until host security, persistence, and plugin activation are accepted as one product package.

recommendation.title: Approve the manifest contract
recommendation.body: Accept the combined PR and treat the documented declaration, precedence, disablement, relative-path, and cross-runtime behavior as the supported plugin API.

likelyOwner.reason: Their history introduced bundle MCP support and recently owns the adjacent Control UI and shared-state foundations, making them the strongest available product-contract owner.
